barCharacter: Vera Oberlin (the high-status judge who rates and dismisses the player; Polly is Pixel's shape-twin for the self-answer and love of a mess, but Vera does Pixel's job). Vera's 12: #12 'my career on not dating losers like you', #45 'such a chore being this beautiful', #46 Cools over Un-Cools, #47 'cover up the literal murder... Right?', #48 'Right. Now.', #49 'since you're SUCH a good advisor...', #50 'most trusted advisor', #51 feminism lecture as an order, #52 scotch, red wine, tears of enemies, poison, #4 'merciless sense of business', #54 cattle prod, #53 'not a death stare this time'. Pixel's 12: thumbnail your own funeral with a red arrow; reported on my alt account; clean run, no deaths, nobody watches those; ending stream before I get bored of ending stream; scored you four out loud, inside it was nine; click the link, horribly, somebody block me; the views, good, me too; skip button, it was me; rare drop, I'm farming these; huge moth, massive moth; screen dimmed to save power; Prince, chat says scam, clicking anyway. (a) Voice: covered, Vera is known by shape alone (a crime or a cruelty taken for granted, then a clipped tag: 'Right?'); Pixel is known mostly by vocabulary (clip, chat, skip, thumbnail). Swap those nouns for Vesper's 'caller' or Maximilian's 'stay' and half of Pixel's best lines change owner. Bar. (b) Construction: Pixel's top 12 are tight, with the turn on the last two to five words, and Vera's 12 include filler ('Come on, think of something!'). Tie. (c) Quotable: Vera's stakes are murder, poison and enemies' tears; Pixel's are views and scores. Only the funeral and alt-account lines reach that level. Bar.

cardHint '{name}, it came down to / somebody did X tonight. Hint/Think about it/Rewatch it/Or didn't.' (21 of 24 could be any star's)

Moving score ticker 'Six, five, ... four' (6 lines)
Pick stamp 'Name. Picked. ...' (12 of 16 pick lines)

ruleBreaks: No line over its word limit, no em dashes, no emoji, no lists, no real person or brand, nothing beyond PG-13.

biggestGap: Pixel has a vocabulary rather than a worldview. Most lines swap a stream noun (clip, chat, skip, score) into an ordinary tease, and nothing real is ever at stake. Vera's lines work because she takes something monstrous for granted. Next pass: for each line, find a real human cost (a funeral, someone crying, a breakup, a fire, a person's dignity) and have Pixel treat it calmly as content, with the stream word as the last-word turn, the way 'You'd thumbnail your own funeral. With a red arrow.' does. Start with the 45 cardHint and holdCard lines, which have neither a stake nor a voice.
